## Introduction {#sec-intro}

This group of pages will present a survey of secondary data at the regional/county level in the Northeast. Note that the graphs and CSV below have been updated to reflect some liberties and consolidation we have done with the framework to make it a bit more presentable. 

## Arrange Datasets

In this section we pull metadata from the secondary metric framework to put together datasets for county/regional analyses. 

To do here:

- Pull revised excel sheet
- Save data paper specific datasets to an object available in this project. 
- This includes data paper meta, data paper tree, and data paper metrics


## Dimension Graphs

```{r}
#| label: prep_graphs
#| include: false
# Filter DF and check data
# source('dev/get_reactable.R')

# Removing soil metrics for now - not suitable for analysis really
tree <- SMdocs::dp_tree %>% 
  mutate(
    indicator = case_when(
        str_detect(indicator, 'inputs bought locally') ~ '% local inputs',
        str_detect(indicator, 'production inputs') ~ 'production inputs',
        str_detect(indicator, 'metabolic') ~ 'presence of disease',
        .default = indicator
      ) %>% 
      str_remove(' of food business'),
    metric = paste0(' ', metric)
  )

# Set up list of results
plots <- list()
```

### Economics

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 12
plots$econ <- SMdocs::get_dimension_ggraph(
  framework_df = tree,
  include_metrics = TRUE,
  dimension_in = 'economics',
  y_limits = c(-3.75, 3.25),
  palette = "scico::batlowW",
  # leaf_font_size = 4.5,
  # index_label_size = 0.2,
  # index_font_size = 4.5,
  arrow = arrow(
    angle = 15,
    length = unit(0.1, 'inches'),
    ends = 'last',
    type = 'closed'
  ) 
)
plots$econ
```

## Sunburst

Little bit messy but maybe fun. Need to fix labels.

```{python}
import plotly.io as pio
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Set renderer to notebook
pio.renderers.default = "notebook_connected"

# Pull data from R
tree = r.tree

# Create plot
px.sunburst(
  tree,
  path=["dimension", "index", "indicator", "metric"]
)
```


## Dimension Table

Easier to interpret table with the framework.

```{r}
dp_tree %>% 
  mutate(metric = case_when(
    str_detect(metric, 'NONE') ~ NA,
    .default = metric
  )) %>% 
  arrange(dimension, index, indicator, metric) %>% 
  get_reactable()
```
